transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-26
- Time: 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Clarity Product Lead), Samir Patel (Clarity ML Eng), Marissa Gomez (Clarity Security)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
Redwood and Clarity Health scoped a POC focused on a triage-assistant workflow. Primary goals: measure quality (hallucination rate, formatting, fidelity), latency and cost at target qps, and establish pass/fail success criteria. Action items include sample data handoff, baseline benchmark, pricing, and compliance checklist.

Topics covered:
- POC success criteria and timelines
- Workload sizing (qps, sequence lengths, concurrency)
- Quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination detection, formatting checks, scoring scheme
- Benchmarks and baseline runs
- Security/compliance gating for Private deployment

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay, thanks everyone for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, Luis is our systems engineer, um goal for today is to walk through the POC scoping and specifically nail down the quality eval plan.
[00:10] Dr. Priya Rao (Customer): great, thanks, we want to confirm what success looks like for us, we have a regulatory-driven use case so hallucination tolerance is basically zero for diagnosis recommendations.
[00:22] Samir (Customer, ML): yeah and on the infra side we care about 50 qps sustained with p95 latency under 400ms if possible, but cost matters; we want to compare hosted vs dedicated options.
[00:35] Luis (Redwood SE): mm-hmm, understood. For the quality plan we usually start with golden prompts and expected outputs - a mix of 200 high-sensitivity prompts and 300 general prompts works well. do you have sample queries?
[00:48] Samir: we can provide 500 examples, I'll anonymize PHI, we have templates for triage and next-step recommendations.
[00:55] Marissa (Security): and we need to validate data residency and KMS integration prior to any real PHI processing. We'll raise a compliance gate.
[01:05] Maya: noted; we'll flag Private deployment as an option. quick question on success criteria: is the acceptance metric purely quality or a mix of quality + latency + cost?
[01:16] Dr. Priya: combination - quality is top-weighted: target is >= 95% format compliance, hallucination rate < 1% on high-sensitivity items, semantic accuracy >= 90% on golden set. Latency p95 < 400ms as Samir said, and cost per 1k tokens under our threshold, we'll share the number after this call.
[01:33] Luis: ok, for scoring approach we propose a multi-metric score: weighted average of FormatCompliance (30%), HallucinationRate inverted (40%), SemanticAccuracy (20%), and Latency penalty (10%). We can share the scoring notebook.
[01:48] Samir: sounds reasonable, can you define how you detect hallucinations? automated heuristics or human review?
[01:56] Luis: good question. We'll do a two-stage approach: automated detection using entity/knowledge checks against the provided ground truth and an initial human spot-check sample for calibration. The automated detector will flag candidate hallucinations for human review; final POC acceptance uses human adjudicated labels.
[02:12] Dr. Priya: that's important - we need audit logs of adjudication and traceability back to prompts and model version.
[02:19] Maya: yes, Redwood can provide traceable eval artifacts; we'll include model version IDs and inference metadata in the eval spreadsheet.
[02:26] [00:02:30] Speaker 1: um can we talk about regression tests? we want to ensure that updates to model or quantization don't degrade critical prompts.
[02:37] Luis: absolutely - we'll set up a regression suite: golden prompts (the 200 high-sensitivity ones) will be included as regression checks, run on every model/quant change during the POC. failures will be triaged with a per-prompt diff and automated alerting.
[02:51] Samir: what's the tolerance for regressions? like one-off vs systemic failures?
[02:56] Luis: we recommend a threshold: no more than 2% regression failures across the golden set per rollout; anything above kicks a rollback. We're flexible on thresholds for the POC and will align to your risk tolerance.
[03:08] Marissa: and for format checks - we need strict JSON Schema compliance for downstream systems. If model outputs a bad JSON it should be counted as failure.
[03:17] Luis: yes, format compliance check against your schema will be automated. We'll validate syntactic JSON first then semantic fields (e.g., diagnosis_code must appear when indicated).
[03:27] Maya: for benchmarking, Luis will run baseline with open model and Redwood-verified config to establish cost/latency numbers. We'll compare hosted CPU/GPU and Dedicated quantized runs.
[03:38] Dr. Priya: timeline wise, when can we get initial baseline?
[03:41] Luis: if we get your 500 samples by Friday (2026-05-01), we can run baseline and share results by Monday-Wednesday following week (2026-05-04 to 05-06).
[03:52] Samir: okay that works. For the POC duration, we were thinking 6 weeks: 1 week ingest and infra, 3 weeks evaluation/iterating, 2 weeks final validation and compliance sign-off.
[04:05] Maya: 6 weeks is standard and reasonable. We'll plan milestones: kickoff, baseline results, mid-POC checkpoint, final report.
[04:13] [00:04:20] Speaker 2: pricing question - hosted vs dedicated cost models and reserved capacity?
[04:19] Maya: we'll send pricing tiers. quick summary: hosted pay-as-you-go, good for short tests; Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Private deployment includes platform fee plus support. We'll include a modeled cost table for your projected qps.
[04:33] Samir: can Redwood run the hallucination/regression detection pipeline on our environment or do samples need to leave our VPC?
[04:41] Luis: for the POC we can run in Redwood hosted with encrypted transit, or in a Private deployment or redwood-managed VPC peering for stricter data controls. For initial tests with anonymized data hosted is simplest; for PHI we strongly recommend Private or dedicated environment with KMS.
[04:58] Marissa: request: include full audit logs and KMS integration before any real PHI.
[05:03] Maya: yes, we'll include compliance artifacts.
[05:08] [00:05:20] Dr. Priya: on scoring details, can you show a worked example? how would you score a single prompt?
[05:16] Luis: sure. example: prompt returns JSON with fields a,b,c. Format compliance passes (1.0). Hallucination detector flags 0.0 for hallucination. Semantic accuracy assessed by human at 0.9. Latency normalized score 0.95. Weighted score = 0.3*1 + 0.4*(1-0) + 0.2*0.9 + 0.1*0.95 = 0.3 + 0.4 + 0.18 + 0.095 = 0.975. This gives a pass; we set pass threshold at 0.9 unless you want higher.
[05:46] Samir: 0.9 seems fine as POC baseline; for production we'll likely tighten.
[05:52] Maya: one more note on golden prompts: we ask that your golden set include edge cases and known tricky phrasing. Redwood will add adversarial paraphrases to stress-test.
[06:05] Dr. Priya: yes, we'll include clinician-written edge cases.
[06:10] [00:06:30] Speaker 3: benchmarking specifics - sequence lengths and tokenization, what's assumed?
[06:16] Luis: we'll profile your inputs: median and 95th percentile sequence lengths. For cost modeling we'll assume avg tokenization based on your samples; please include both short triage prompts (~40 tokens) and longer context ones (400+ tokens). Also tell us concurrency targets (50 qps was mentioned).
[06:33] Samir: concurrence of 50 qps at peak but steady-state might be 10-20 qps; most requests are short though 10-15% include full encounter notes.
[06:44] Luis: perfect - we'll include both in the benchmark.
[06:48] Maya: about hallucination labelling: we propose a small human study - 50 sampled responses per model variant for adjudication. That gives confidence intervals for hallucination estimates.
[06:58] Dr. Priya: sounds good; what's the projected human review cost?
[07:02] Luis: small - we typically estimate 1-2 hours of annotation for 50 samples with a clinician reviewer; we can include that in the cost table.
[07:10] [00:07:30] Speaker 1: any concerns about model rollouts or quantization-induced regressions?
[07:16] Luis: yes, quantization can affect some rare tokens and formatting; that's why regression checks on golden prompts and format schema are required after any model/quant change. We can automate canary rollouts and rollback.
[07:27] Samir: can we lock a model version for the POC?
[07:30] Maya: yes, we'll pin to a model version and only change under agreed rollouts.
[07:34] Marissa: we also need RBAC for who can trigger rollouts and access logs.
[07:38] Maya: Redwood supports RBAC and SSO/SAML; we'll include role mappings in the compliance doc.
[07:45] [00:08:00] Luis: on outputs we will also run structural validators - if JSON fails schema it counts as a hard fail for that prompt; we'll collect examples and cluster failure modes to help engineers fix prompts or add constraints.
[08:00] Dr. Priya: what about hallucinations that are subtle - e.g., wrong medication name but plausible?
[08:06] Luis: those are caught by entity-level checks against ground truth and human adjudication. We'll also compute precision/recall for entity extraction.
[08:15] Samir: for the POC report can you include per-prompt breakdown, aggregate metrics, and recommended remediation steps?
[08:20] Maya: yes, final report will include per-prompt logs, aggregated scores, latency/cost curves, and remediation recommendations.
[08:27] [00:08:40] Speaker 2: timeline recap?
[08:30] Maya: recap: 1) Clarity to send 500 anonymized samples + schema by 2026-05-01. 2) Redwood SE baseline run and share spreadsheet by 2026-05-04. 3) Kickoff POC infra week of 2026-05-11. 4) Mid-POC checkpoint week 3. 5) Final report and compliance artifacts by end of POC (~6 weeks).
[08:52] Marissa: we'll review compliance artifacts during mid-POC and finalize KMS/SSO before accepting PHI flows.
[08:59] Samir: what about the eval automation - can we run the same tests periodically post-POC?
[09:04] Luis: yes, Redwood can export the eval pipeline as a runnable job in your environment or host it and provide access; we'll propose both options.
[09:12] Dr. Priya: sounds good. one last question - for hallucination threshold <1% on high-sensitivity, do you have confidence intervals? we want to ensure statistical significance.
[09:22] Luis: with 200 high-sensitivity prompts, observing 1% (2 errors) gives fairly wide CI; we'll provide power calculations and can increase sample size if you want tighter bounds - e.g., 500 would shrink CI.
[09:34] Maya: we'll include recommended sample sizes in the eval plan doc.
[09:38] [00:09:50] Speaker 1: ok, next steps and owners are captured. thanks everyone.
[09:44] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with pricing, the eval spreadsheet link (placeholder: https://redwood.internal/eval/CRM-45812-baseline), and the scoring notebook.
[09:55] Samir: thanks all, we'll get samples in by Friday.
[10:00] Meeting ended.

Loose notes / references mentioned during call:
- Eval spreadsheet link (shared by Redwood): https://redwood.internal/eval/CRM-45812-baseline
- Scoring notebook (will be shared): internal link promised by Luis
- Compliance checklist template (Redwood CISO pack)

Closing recap (from Maya):
- Success criteria: >=95% format compliance, hallucination rate <1% on high-sensitivity golden set, semantic accuracy >=90%; latency p95 <400ms; cost target TBD by Clarity
- Golden prompts: Clarity to supply 500 total, with 200 labeled high-sensitivity for the golden/regression set; Redwood to add adversarial paraphrases
- Regression tests: run on every model/quant change, threshold recommended 2% failures on golden set to trigger rollback
- Hallucination checks: automated detector + human adjudication sample (50 per variant) for final acceptance
- Scoring approach: weighted metrics (Format 30%, Hallucination 40%, Semantic 20%, Latency 10%) with pass threshold 0.9 for POC

End of transcript.
